text.p: NCR Corp. said Wednesday that it cut its first-quarter loss by 75 percent as it reduced expenses and improved margins, although the strong dollar and a change in marketing strategy hurt overall results.
NCR's stock fell by $2.375, or more than 7 percent, to $29.75 in afternoon trading on the New York Stock Exchange.

The manufacturer of computers and other business machines, which was spun off by AT&T Corp. at the end of last year, said its loss for the three months ended March 31 narrowed to $16 million, or 16 cents a share, from $65 million, or 64 cents a share, in the year-ago period.
The company, which is based in Dayton, Ohio, added that its revenue for the quarter declined 12 percent to $1.39 billion from $1.59 billion last year.

"Our first-quarter results were impacted by external factors that included the strong U.S. dollar and continued weakness in European markets," Chairman Lars Nyberg said in a statement. "In addition, the decision to no longer sell PCs through high-volume retail channels further reduced revenue compared to the year-ago quarter."
NCR said its gross margins increased to 27.6 percent of revenues from 25.5 percent and its operating loss for the quarter narrowed to $18 million from $37 million.
The company also said its orders increased over last year's first quarter.
"The quarter's strong incoming order pattern, which exceeded our objectives on a local currency basis, gives us confidence about achieving revenue growth in subsequent quarters," Nyberg said.
"We continue to be encouraged by operational improvements in gross margins and expenses," he added.
